title: Property Deposits in Vietnam 2026: Deposit Contracts and Forfeiture
desc: Property deposits under the Civil Code: what a deposit contract should state, when the deposit is lost or doubled, and the 5% cap for project homes.
summary: The rules on deposits when buying or selling property under the Civil Code 2015: contents of a deposit contract, the forfeiture principle and what to check before paying.
body: p

Almost every property transaction starts with a deposit. If the deposit paper is sloppy, a dispute is very likely when one side changes its mind. This article summarises the rules on deposits under Article 328 of the Civil Code 2015 and what should be stated clearly in a deposit contract.
h2
1. What is a deposit?
p

A deposit is when the depositor gives the deposit recipient a sum of money (or precious metal, gemstones or other valuables) for a set period to secure the entry into or performance of a contract (Clause 1, Article 328). A deposit is one of the measures to secure performance of obligations (Article 292).
p
When the sale contract is signed and performed, the deposit is returned to the depositor or offset against the purchase price (Clause 2, Article 328).
h2
2. Forfeiture: whoever changes their mind bears the loss
ul
The buyer (depositor) refuses to sign or perform the contract: the deposit belongs to the seller.
The seller (deposit recipient) refuses: must return the deposit plus an amount equal to the deposit. For example, on a VND 100 million deposit, VND 200 million must be paid.
The two parties may agree otherwise (for example a higher forfeiture amount, or cases in which the deposit is returned) – Clause 2, Article 328.
p

Besides deposit forfeiture, the parties may also agree on a contractual penalty; if they want the breaching party to both pay the penalty and compensate for damage, this must be stated expressly, otherwise only the penalty applies (Article 418).
h2
3. Must a deposit contract be notarised?
p

The Civil Code allows transactions to be made orally, in writing or by conduct; notarisation or certification is required only where the law so provides (Article 119). The documents in our library contain no rule requiring a deposit contract to be notarised; even so, it is advisable to make it in writing, with a witness or notarisation if the amount is large. A contract is valid only if the parties have capacity, act entirely voluntarily and the content does not violate the law (Article 117).
p
The sale or transfer contract for the property signed afterwards must, however, be notarised or certified – see Notarising Property Sale Contracts 2026.
h2
4. What should a deposit contract state?
ol
Full names and ID numbers of the parties; if the property is under joint names (spouses, several people), all must sign or there must be a power of attorney (Clause 2, Article 27 of the Land Law).
Property details as on the Certificate: plot number, map sheet, area and address.
The sale price, deposit amount and how the balance is paid.
The deadline for signing the sale contract at a notary office.
Who pays personal income tax, registration fee and notarisation fee.
Cases in which the deposit is returned without penalty (for example the property is under distraint, in dispute or ineligible for transfer).
The forfeiture amount, contractual penalty and how disputes are resolved.
h2
5. Buying a project home: deposit capped at 5%
p

For off-plan housing, the investor may collect a deposit of no more than 5% of the selling price, and only once the housing meets the conditions to be put into business (Clause 5, Article 23 of the Law on Real Estate Business). See also Buying Off-Plan Housing 2026.
h2
6. When a dispute arises
p

The breaching party must compensate for all damage unless otherwise agreed (Article 360). The limitation period for suing over a contract dispute is 3 years from the date the person knew or should have known that their rights were infringed (Article 429). Before paying a deposit, check that the property meets the conditions for transaction – see Conditions for Housing to Be Sold or Gifted.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The Land Law 2024 and the Law on Real Estate Business 2023 are currently partially no longer in effect; for high-value transactions, have a lawyer or notary draft the deposit contract.
